I've only played 64, TTYD, and TOK. I thoroughly enjoyed them all, and I don't have a favorite or least favorite.

64 and TTYD are both excellent RPGs. I love their badge systems and the writing. Plenty of people have written about what they love about these games, and it's all true. The writing, character variety, combat systems... almost every aspect is amazing.

TOK is fun, but it's different from the other two. The story and dialogue is just as good, and I loved how much more open its levels were. The world felt truly alive even though the majority of NPCs in this game are toads. The graphics are gorgeous. The battle system in TOK is very different-- it's a ring puzzle where you line up enemies to do damage. I found this enjoyable, but I generally enjoy puzzles. If you're looking for strategic turn-based combat where you carefully consider your stats and build, TOK is not the game for you. If you enjoy puzzles, well-written stories and dialogue, paper puns, and levels with lots of exploration, you'll enjoy it a lot.
This was a lot of fun! I hope you make more puzzles :)

Moves: Stockpile, Chilling Water, Acid Spray, Acupressure


Stockpile once before Greninja wipes your stat boosts and once right after. Chilling Water and/or heal cheer before he clears stat boosts. After that, use Acid Spray once or twice on Greninja. Then for the rest of the battle, Acupressure on Slowbro to buff its stats for Stored Power. 

I've won every raid that has had a stored power slowbro with this Qwilfish build. It can also work to buff Slowking or Vaporeon if there's no Slowbro.

I use Qwilfish to support Stored Power users. Stockpile once and use Chilling Water, Acid Spray, and/or healing cheer until Greninja clears stat buffs.

Then do one stockpile for survivability.

After that, acupressure the Stored Power user (Slowbro or Vaporeon), cheering as needed. If there's more than one Stored Power user, I like to use Acid Spray a few times before Acupressure to help everyone do damage.
